title: Reaction types, including oxidation-reduction
blurb: Classify synthesis, decomposition, replacement, combustion and neutralization reactions, and find what is oxidized, what is reduced and which agent does each.
question: In Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, a gray zinc strip becomes coated with copper. What type of reaction is this, which substance is oxidized, and which is the oxidizing agent?

teach.body: Formally, reactions are classified by how reactants rearrange into products. In plain English: look at what goes in and what comes out, and match the shape. Is there one reactant or one product? Is a lone element swapping into a compound? Is a fuel burning in oxygen? Most HESI reaction items come down to spotting that shape, then asking who lost electrons and who gained them.

head: Type
Pattern
Example
teach.caption: Neutralization is a special double replacement. A double replacement often forms a precipitate (solid AgCl), a gas or water.

teach.h: Classify by looking at the reactants
Single replacement needs a more active element
teach.body: In A + BC → AC + B, the free element A replaces B only if A is more reactive. Zinc is more active than copper, so zinc in copper(II) sulfate gives ZnSO₄ and copper metal; copper in zinc sulfate does nothing. Copper is more active than silver, so a copper wire in silver nitrate grows silver crystals. Halogens follow the same idea: Cl₂ replaces bromine in NaBr.

Formally, oxidation is the loss of electrons and reduction is the gain of electrons. In plain English: electrons move from one substance to another, so whatever one loses, the other gains, and the two always happen together (redox). Older definitions still appear: oxidation as gaining oxygen or losing hydrogen, reduction as losing oxygen or gaining hydrogen. Rusting, combustion, cellular respiration and batteries are all redox.

teach.caption: Or: LEO the lion says GER (Lose Electrons Oxidation, Gain Electrons Reduction).

head: Rule
Value
Example
teach.caption: Oxidation number goes UP: oxidized. Goes DOWN: reduced.
The agent is named for what it does to the OTHER substance: the reducing agent is itself oxidized.

teach.body: Daniel, a respiratory therapy applicant, studies rusting: 4 Fe + 3 O₂ → 2 Fe₂O₃. Free iron is 0. In Fe₂O₃, 2 Fe + 3(−2) = 0, so each Fe is +3: iron's number rose, so iron is oxidized and is the reducing agent. Oxygen went from 0 in O₂ to −2: reduced, the oxidizing agent. It is also a synthesis reaction: two reactants, one product.

teach.text: Oxidation is LOSS of electrons, not gain. The oxidizing agent is REDUCED (it takes electrons); the reducing agent is OXIDIZED. Free elements are 0, whatever their usual ion charge. Oxygen is −1 in peroxides. Redox does not need oxygen: 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl is redox. And AB + CD → AD + CB is DOUBLE replacement, not single.

items: Synthesis A + B → AB; decomposition AB → A + B; single A + BC → AC + B; double AB + CD → AD + CB.
Combustion: fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Neutralization: acid + base → salt + water.
A free element replaces a less active one: Zn replaces Cu; Cu replaces Ag.
OIL RIG: oxidation is loss of electrons (number up); reduction is gain (number down).
Substance oxidized = reducing agent; substance reduced = oxidizing agent.

summary: You can now classify synthesis, decomposition, single and double replacement, combustion and neutralization reactions and predict single replacement from relative activity. You can also assign oxidation numbers and name what is oxidized, what is reduced and which substance is the oxidizing or reducing agent.

A.q: Which type of reaction is Zn + 2 HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂?
A.why: A free element (Zn) replaces another element (H) in a compound: A + BC → AC + B.

whyNot.0: Synthesis combines reactants into one product; here there are two products.
whyNot.2: Double replacement needs two compounds swapping partners; zinc is a free element.
whyNot.3: Decomposition starts with a single compound breaking apart.

A.q: Which type of reaction is 2 KClO₃ → 2 KCl + 3 O₂?
A.why: One compound breaks down into simpler substances: AB → A + B.

whyNot.1: Synthesis is the reverse: several reactants forming one product.
whyNot.2: Combustion consumes O₂ and a fuel; here O₂ is produced.
whyNot.3: Single replacement needs a free element and a compound as reactants.

A.q: In a redox reaction, what happens to the substance that is oxidized?
A.why: Oxidation is loss of electrons (OIL RIG), so the oxidation number rises.

whyNot.1: Gaining protons describes a base in acid-base chemistry, not oxidation.
whyNot.2: Protons stay in the nucleus during chemical reactions; redox moves electrons.

B.q: Which type of reaction is BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ + 2 NaCl?
B.why: Two compounds exchange partners (AB + CD → AD + CB), and solid BaSO₄ precipitates.

whyNot.0: Single replacement needs a free element; both reactants here are compounds.
whyNot.1: Synthesis gives one product; this reaction gives two.
whyNot.3: Decomposition starts with one reactant; there are two here.

B.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?

whyNot.1: +4 would fit MnO₂; in KMnO₄ the four oxygens total −8.
whyNot.3: −7 has the wrong sign; manganese must offset the oxygens' negative total.

B.q: In 2 Mg + O₂ → 2 MgO, which statement is correct?
options: Mg is reduced; O₂ is the reducing agent
Mg is oxidized; O₂ is the reducing agent
Mg is oxidized; O₂ is the oxidizing agent
Mg is reduced; O₂ is the oxidizing agent
B.why: Mg goes 0 → +2 (loses electrons, oxidized). O goes 0 → −2 (gains electrons, reduced), so O₂ is the oxidizing agent.

whyNot.0: Magnesium's oxidation number rises, so it is oxidized, not reduced.
whyNot.1: O₂ is reduced, which makes it the oxidizing agent.
whyNot.3: O₂ is the oxidizing agent, but magnesium loses electrons, so it is oxidized.

C.q: An iron nail is placed in copper(II) sulfate solution, and copper metal forms on the nail. Which statement best explains this?
options: Copper is more active, so it replaces iron
Iron is more active, so it replaces copper
Sulfate ions are reduced to sulfur metal
Iron and copper combine in a synthesis
C.why: Single replacement: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. The free metal replaces copper because iron is more active.

whyNot.0: If copper were more active, the iron nail would not displace it; the free element is the more active one.
whyNot.2: Sulfate stays as SO₄²⁻ in FeSO₄; copper ions are the ones reduced.
whyNot.3: There are two products, FeSO₄ and Cu, so this is not synthesis.

C.q: What is the oxidation number of chromium in the dichromate ion, Cr₂O₇²⁻?
C.why: The sum equals the ion's charge: 2Cr + 7(−2) = −2, so 2Cr = +12 and Cr = +6.

whyNot.0: +7 sets the sum to 0 (2Cr = +14); the sum must equal the ion's charge, −2.
whyNot.1: +12 is the total for both chromium atoms; divide by 2.
whyNot.3: +14 is the total for both Cr atoms with the −2 charge ignored; it is not one atom's number.

C.q: In Fe₂O₃ + 3 CO → 2 Fe + 3 CO₂, which substance is the reducing agent?
options: Fe₂O₃, because its iron is reduced
CO₂, because it gains an oxygen
Fe, because it becomes a metal
CO, because its carbon is oxidized
C.why: Carbon goes from +2 in CO to +4 in CO₂: it is oxidized, so CO is the reducing agent. Iron goes +3 → 0 (reduced), so Fe₂O₃ is the oxidizing agent.

whyNot.0: Fe₂O₃ is reduced, which makes it the oxidizing agent.
whyNot.1: CO₂ is a product; agents are reactants.
whyNot.2: Fe is a product formed by reduction, not the agent.

reteach.title: Passing a ball
reteach.question: Two teammates pass a ball: one throws it, the other catches it. How does that match oxidation and reduction?

blocks.body: The thrower loses the ball: oxidized. The catcher gains it: reduced. There is no throw without a catch, so oxidation and reduction always happen together. The thrower makes the catch possible, so the thrower is the reducing agent; the catcher pulls the ball in, so the catcher is the oxidizing agent. Each player is named for what they do to the other one.

blocks.text: The oxidizing agent is not the one that gets oxidized. It is the catcher: it takes the electrons and is reduced.

explain.body: Synthesis (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), single replacement (A + BC → AC + B), double replacement (AB + CD → AD + CB), combustion (fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O) and neutralization (acid + base → salt + water).

test.q: Which type of reaction is CH₄ + 2 O₂ → CO₂ + 2 H₂O?
test.why: A hydrocarbon fuel reacts with oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water: combustion.

whyNot.0: Synthesis produces a single product; this reaction has two.
whyNot.2: Decomposition starts from one compound breaking apart; here methane reacts with oxygen.
whyNot.3: O₂ is an element, not a compound, and the CO₂ + H₂O products mark combustion.

explain.body: A free element replaces another in a compound only if it is more active. Zinc replaces copper; copper replaces silver. Chlorine replaces bromine in a bromide salt.

explain.caption: A metal can replace any metal to its right in this list.

test.q: Which pair will react when the metal is placed in the solution?
test.why: Zinc is more active than copper, so it replaces copper: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu.

whyNot.0: Copper is less active than zinc, so it cannot replace zinc.
whyNot.1: Silver is less active than copper, so it cannot replace copper.
whyNot.3: Copper is less active than iron, so it cannot replace iron.

explain.body: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons; Reduction Is Gain. One cannot happen without the other: electrons lost by one substance are gained by another.

test.q: In 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl, what happens to chlorine?
options: It is oxidized by losing electrons
It is reduced by gaining electrons
It is oxidized by gaining electrons
It is reduced by losing electrons
test.why: Each chlorine atom gains an electron from sodium to become Cl⁻. Gain of electrons is reduction.

whyNot.0: Sodium is the one that loses electrons; chlorine gains them.
whyNot.2: Gaining electrons is reduction, not oxidation.
whyNot.3: Chlorine gains electrons; losing them would be oxidation.

explain.body: Free elements are 0; oxygen is usually −2; hydrogen +1; the total equals the charge. A rising number means oxidized (the reducing agent); a falling number means reduced (the oxidizing agent).

items.label: any free element: Fe, O₂, Cl₂

test.q: In Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which substance is the oxidizing agent?
test.why: Cu²⁺ gains 2 electrons (+2 → 0), so it is reduced. The substance reduced is the oxidizing agent.

whyNot.0: Zinc is oxidized (0 → +2), so it is the reducing agent.
whyNot.2: Zn²⁺ is a product; the agents are reactants.
whyNot.3: Cu is the product formed when Cu²⁺ is reduced, not the agent.
